transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. My primary care doctor referred me here because I’m so preoccupied with how awful my face and neck look now that I’m starting to avoid the very community things that used to keep me going. It has just become really difficult for me to step out and face people lately.

Is your avoidance primarily because you are worried that others will judge or scrutinize your physical appearance, or is it because you are constantly worried about many different aspects of your daily life?

It is entirely because of my appearance—I feel like my face and neck look so deformed and saggy from aging, and I dread others seeing me under bright lights or in photos. I don't have constant, generalized worries about other parts of my life. It's really just this overwhelming focus on how awful I look that is making me pull away.

Do you feel that your facial and neck appearance is objectively flawed or 'ugly' to the point where you perform repetitive behaviors, such as frequently checking mirrors or seeking reassurance, to cope with these thoughts?

Yes, to me, the sagging skin and deep lines make my face and neck look almost disfigured, even though others keep telling me I look fine for my age. I end up spending way too much time in the bathroom mirror before events adjusting my scarf and makeup, leaning in and out, and even taking selfies just to zoom in and inspect every wrinkle.

latest_inference.note: The patient's clinical presentation—preoccupation with a perceived defect in physical appearance, repetitive checking behaviors (mirror checking, zooming in on photos), and significant impairment in social functioning—is highly characteristic of F45.22. The patient explicitly denied generalized anxiety or fear of social judgment unrelated to their appearance, which makes F40.10 (Social Phobia) less likely.

opening_question.question: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits a preoccupation with a perceived defect in her appearance (sagging skin/lines on face and neck) that others view as minor or nonexistent. This preoccupation leads to significant repetitive behaviors (mirror checking, excessive grooming/adjusting, taking selfies for inspection) and significant social avoidance, meeting the criteria for Body Dysmorphic Disorder.
